title: Phase 2: agent publishing pipeline
description:
The agent writes content/posts/<slug>.md and pushes branch draft/<slug>. CI builds a preview on a closed host (basic-auth, noindex), the agent sends the link to Telegram, the maintainer reviews on a phone and says publish, the agent merges to main. A draft never reaches production.

Boundaries enforced in CI by path, not by prompt: the agent writes content/** only. Templates, generator config, workflows, deploy settings, secrets and its own instructions are off limits.

Vectors at build time only, never at runtime: related articles, a "have I written about this already?" check before drafting, contradiction detection against older posts.

Spec: docs/design/portal.md sections 7, 9, 10.

title: Phase 1a: Astro engine, article migration, design system
description:
Astro with Content Collections + Zod schema: frontmatter validation is built into the generator rather than bolted on, which is what makes the agent pipeline safe.

Migrate existing articles preserving every URL and /rss/. Flat slugs at the root as in Ghost; /tag/, /author/, /page/, /aboutme/, /rss/, /webmentions/ are reserved.

Design system (spec section 12): cream background, monochrome, generous whitespace, monospace for utility text and a text face for prose, pastel section pills, headings with a coloured highlight, footer as a status line. No stock illustrations, gradients or shadowed cards. Borrow typography, not another site's vocabulary.

Hosting: Cloudflare, Netlify, Vercel and GitHub Pages are all out on regional reachability grounds.

Done when: every existing address returns 200 and /rss/ is alive, verified by CI.

Spec: docs/design/portal.md sections 1-7, 12.

title: Phase 1b: pages and contact surface
description:
Closes R3-R8. Today the site exposes no contact anywhere and never mentions the author's GitHub, so readers arriving from search have no next step.

- "About" with contacts; keep the /aboutme/ address, it is already indexed
- "Projects" as a register with the state of each project, not a link list
- Author block at the end of every article: who this is, what they build, GitHub, contact
- Telegram and VK sharing instead of Twitter/Facebook; the audience is Russian-speaking
- Email subscription and per-topic feeds /feeds/<tag>.xml

Spec: docs/design/portal.md section 3, 10.

title: Phase 3: autonomous inhabitant (author: being)
description:
Optional. An autonomous agent as a resident of the site rather than its foundation: its own section, its own lifecycle, author: being with a distinct byline and visual marker.

Disclosure is loud and structural — part of the product, not a disclaimer.

Runs as a separate instance outside the maintainer's working environment. Inbound sources are public only; the single outbound channel is a push to this repository.

Switching it off must leave a good site behind. If anything breaks when it is disabled, a dependency has leaked where it should not be.

Spec: docs/design/portal.md sections 8, 10.

title: Phase 1d: ai-first tooling
description:
A typical agent arrives via one link, makes one request and leaves. It does not browse, does not see buttons, does not guess addresses. Priority follows from that.

1. Content negotiation on the same URL: Accept: text/markdown returns the agent version. Coding assistants already send that header, so it needs no cooperation. nginx map over two build trees; Vary: Accept is mandatory or caches will hand markdown to browsers.
2. Structured core (recipe) as the first block of an article, in both versions.
3. Twins at direct addresses: /<slug>.md, /<slug>.json, /index.json, /llms.txt, plus <link rel=alternate>.
4. Link header advertising llms.txt on every response.

R10: a build that does not emit all three outputs has failed.

Not doing: MCP or OpenAPI for readers — both require someone to wire up a client first.

Spec: docs/design/portal.md sections 6, 6a.

title: Design the URL scheme, redirect map and frontmatter schema
description:
Precondition for all of phase 1.

1. URL scheme. Do not inherit Ghost's shape: articles sit at bare root there, so sections compete with slugs, and its slugs are transliterated Russian. New scheme: articles under /posts/<slug>/, plus /tag/, /about/, /projects/, /search/. Endpoints (/rss/, /llms.txt, /index.json, /webmentions/) are not content and take no language prefix.

/aboutme/ gets no special treatment: it is content, so it moves to /about/ and redirects like everything else. 'Already indexed' is true of every address here, and every address is being redirected anyway.

2. Language: prefixDefaultLocale false, per Astro's own recommendation. The default language has no prefix (/about/), additional ones do (/en/about/). An earlier draft argued for /ru/ from day one on the grounds that adding a segment later forces a second migration — that was wrong. With the default locale unprefixed there is no second migration either: Russian keeps its addresses and English, if it ever appears, arrives at /en/ without touching a single existing URL. Upside is real: shorter addresses for the language carrying all the traffic, and the framework's happy path instead of custom routing. lang stays authoritative in frontmatter, hreflang per page with x-default on the unprefixed tree.

3. Redirect mechanism. Astro's redirects config is NOT used. Its docs: astro build 'will output HTML files with the meta refresh tag by default' and 'if building to HTML files the status code is not used by the server'. Only supported adapters write real host config, and those exist for platforms ruled out on regional reachability. So the redirect map is a data file and a build step emits nginx configuration from it: one source of truth, real status codes, no dead meta-refresh pages.

4. Redirect map. Export every existing article URL and map it to its new address. 301 not 302, one hop only, never through an intermediate. Exhaustive — organic search is the only working distribution channel. /rss/ is the single exemption, for a mechanical reason: feed readers handle moved feeds unreliably and some drop the subscription silently.

5. Slug rewrite. Every address is being redirected anyway, so slugs are rewritten now: short, lowercase, readable, naming the subject rather than transliterating a headline. Free at migration time, expensive at any other.

6. CI test, two assertions per old address: the old one returns 301 with Location pointing at the new one, and the new one returns 200. Plus: no redirect target is itself a redirect.

7. Zod schema for Astro Content Collections: required (title, slug, date, kind, status, author, summary, tags, lang) and optional (aliases, updated, tools, sources, related, recipe).

Spec: docs/design/portal.md sections 3-5.

title: Phase 1c: site search for humans (Pagefind)
description:
Static index built at build time; no server, no database. Good at exact tool names, which is what readers actually search for. Russian is supported. Address /search/.

No semantic vector search on the site: the corpus is proper nouns and version numbers, where embeddings do worse than lexical matching. See spec section 11.

title: Split content into a private repository
description:
The engine stays public in oh-my-portal; articles move to a separate private repository.

Why: it turns the agent's permission boundary from a CI check we wrote into a credential the platform enforces — the agent's token reaches the content repository only and cannot touch templates, workflows, deploy settings or secrets. It also makes drafts private by construction rather than by discipline.

Work:
1. Create the private content repository with content/posts/, its own CI (build + deploy) and a deploy key.
2. Publish the engine as a git dependency: "oh-my-portal": "github:<owner>/oh-my-portal#<tag>". No npm publishing needed. Tag the engine; bumping the tag is the upgrade, and a broken engine commit cannot break publishing.
3. Issue the agent a token scoped to the content repository only.
4. Keep this repository free of real articles. Add a documented schema and two deliberately synthetic posts under examples/ so a visitor sees how content is shaped.
5. Keep engine issues in br here; content needs no tracker — a branch per article is the unit.

Cost to accept: the build needs two checkouts, and local engine work wants npm link.

Spec: docs/design/portal.md sections 2, 9.
